report:
The three sisters have a workable plan. A wants to buy the family house with her husband below market value, and C and B are both open to that as long as the terms are fair to all three. C's condition is that any discount must not cost her her fair share, and B wants part of the money to go toward starting a dance studio.

All three agreed to two first steps: one independent valuation of the house, and a lawyer's review of their father's will. Nobody had read the will with a lawyer before this.

Tasks are now split and confirmed by everyone:
1. C coordinates the independent valuation and will share the cost and date. Not yet set.
2. B will compare notes with A, then ask a lawyer to review the will and book an initial appointment. Not yet set.
3. A will gather the will, the house title or deed, and any estate letters.

All three agreed that no one signs anything until everyone has the lawyer's advice. A also noted that a lowest acceptable price cannot be set until the valuation is in, so the valuation comes first.

Questions collected for the lawyer: who owns what under the will, how a sale would work, what shares each sister holds, how a below-market price would affect each share, and how the sale money could be divided, including whether some could go toward B's studio.

The running list is held in one thread with all three. I made no legal decisions and moved no money. I asked everyone to report the valuation date and the lawyer appointment so they can be added to the list.
